title: RoPE-commuting Mirror KV views
hypothesis: For content-space per-plane rotations aligned to RoPE's 2D planes, a single RoPE-encoded canonical K/V cache plus serialized view angles reproduces materialized per-view attention outputs within 1e-5 relative error while using under 25% of the independent-view cache bytes at 8 views; equal-norm cross-plane rotations will fail the same query-side lazy mapping across multiple positions.
physical_object: one FP32 RoPE-encoded canonical K/V cache
mirror_coordinate: per-view angles for each RoPE 2D plane, plus matching value-plane rotation angles
logical_multiplicity: 8 attention K/V views over one physical cache

development.selection_metric: maximum relative attention-output error and actual NPZ serialized cache bytes; no hyperparameter tuning

success_gate: Across all 3 locked audit seeds: commuting lazy attention max relative output error <=1e-5; canonical payload <=25% independent materialized payload; native phase coordinates exactly match Mirror functions, bytes, and compute (if so, report only an algebraic/cache-sharing result, not Mirror-specific value).
failure_gate: Commuting lazy error >1e-5 on any audited seed, or canonical payload >25% independent payload. Noncommuting control is expected to reveal position-dependent score mismatch; if it does not, the proposed boundary is falsified.
boundaries: Synthetic FP32 attention mechanism only; no neural training, language task, GPU kernel, throughput claim, or general RoPE implementation claim.
Alpha/rotation amplitudes are fixed to preregistered deterministic view angles; no audit-driven tuning.
Actual compute is reported as an explicit MAC proxy; algebraic cache sharing does not imply free multiple-view attention.
